question.text: There are four numbers of which the first three are in GP and the last three are in AP, whose common difference is 6 . If the first and the last numbers are equal, then two other numbers are

solution.text:
Let 3 numbers in AP are $a,(a+6),(a+12)$
Also, first and last number out of 4 numbers are equal $\therefore 4$ numbers are $(a+12), a,(a+6),(a+12)$
Also, given, first 3 numbers are in GP
$\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & a^2=(a+12)(a+6) \\
\Rightarrow & a^2=a^2+18 a+72 \\
\Rightarrow & a=-\frac{72}{18}=-4
\end{array}$
$\therefore 4$ numbers are $8,-4,2,8$
